diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any $\epsilon>0$, the operator $\mathcal{T}_{\epsilon,\#}$ is positive, because $|S(x)| \geq c_\epsilon >0$ for all $x \in \overline{D} \backslash \overline{Y}_\epsilon$.

issues.failure_explanation: The range identity in Theorem A.1 requires T_# coercive. The assumption |S|>0 a.e. allows S to vanish on a set of measure zero (e.g., an isolated point), so T_# is not bounded below. Norm convergence of F_epsilon to F does not imply the ranges of their square roots converge to Range(F_#^{1/2}); the limit is only a dense subspace. Thus the equality can fail; Range(F_#^{1/2}) is generally strictly smaller than Range(L).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore a coercivity condition, e.g., assume |S|>=c>0 on D, or replace the equality with an appropriately justified range characterization that accounts for non-coercive T_# and adjust the indicator functions.
issues.overall_effect: Invalidates the claimed range identity under the weakened source assumption and all subsequent range-based strip and uniqueness results.
issues.title: Range identity fails without coercivity of T
issues.why_classification: Excluding the advertised a.e. positivity regime and losing the central range identity is a major loss; no comparable result survives under the stated hypotheses without new arguments.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $z \in {K}_{D,\eta}^{(\hat{x})}$, then there exists $y\in {D}$ such that ${b_{z,\eta}^{(\hat{x})}}=c^{-1}\hat{x}\cdot y -t_0$. Choose the set $\{y_m\}_{m=1}^{\infty}$ such that $y=y_1$.Then we have $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L_N)$ for all $N\geq 1$. By Lemma \ref{lem4.1} (ii), it holds that $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.failure_explanation: For fixed \hat x, L maps u in L^2(D) to the Fourier transform of an L^2 function supported in the projection interval. The test function e^{-i tau b} corresponds to the Fourier transform of a delta at b, not an L^2 function, so it is not in Range(L) even when b lies in the interval. The proof's finite-dimensional ranges L_N are finite spans of exponentials; their union is not equal to Range(L). The inverse Fourier transform of e^{-i tau b} on (0,K) is not a delta. Thus the iff characterization is false, and the pointwise test function method lacks a rigorous foundation.

failure_location.quote: For any $\eta \in \R$, there holds $z \in {K}_{D,\eta}^{(\hat{x})}$ if and only if $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the pointwise test functions by test functions known to lie in Range(L) (e.g., integrated over small spatial domains as in earlier factorization approaches) and rederive the indicator and uniqueness results; alternatively, establish a different range characterization for pointwise exponentials if possible.
issues.overall_effect: Invalidates the main strip characterization, indicator functions, determination of t0, and uniqueness results that rely on pointwise test functions.
issues.title: Pointwise test functions are not in Range(L)
issues.why_classification: The central theorem of the paper is false; repairing it requires changing the test function construction and re-proving the main inversion scheme, a new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Range(L_N) is the finite span of exponentials e^{-i tau a_m}. The union over N is a set of finite linear combinations of such exponentials, whose inverse Fourier transforms are discrete measures. Range(L) consists of Fourier transforms of L^2 functions supported in the projection interval. These sets are not equal (except zero); the union is at most dense in L^2(0,K). Thus the equality used to prove Theorem lem3.4 is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the equality by a correct density statement and supply a different argument that does not require pointwise exponentials to lie exactly in Range(L); this entails reworking the proof of Theorem lem3.4.
issues.overall_effect: Invalidates the proof of the test-function range characterization and all results depending on it.
issues.title: False equality Range(L)=lim Range(L_N)
issues.why_classification: The false equality is central to the proof of the main test-function theorem; no local correction preserves the intended exact range characterization.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Denoting by  $\left\{ ( {\tilde \lambda^{( x)}_n}, \psi^{(x)}_n): n=1,2,\cdots,N \right\}$ an eigen-system of the matrix $F^{(\hat x)}$ (\ref{matF})
In another way,  we may also use the \textcolor{ghx}{SPD} discrete approximation $(F^{(\hat x)})_\#$.

issues.failure_explanation: The matrices Re(F) and Im(F) generally do not commute, so an eigenvector of F is not necessarily an eigenvector of |Re(F)| or |Im(F)|. The eigenvalues of |Re(F)|+|Im(F)| are not given by |Re lambda|+|Im lambda| for eigenvalues lambda of F. A counterexample is F=[[1,i],[0,2]], whose eigenvalues are 1 and 2, while F_#=diag(1,3) has eigenvalues 1 and 3. Thus the described eigendecomposition is incorrect.

failure_location.quote: then one deduces that  an eigen-system of the matrix $(F^{(\hat x)})_\#:= |\real (F^{(\hat x)})|+|\ima(F^{(\hat x)})|$ is $\left\{ ( \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n, \psi^{(\hat x)}_n): n=1,2,\cdots,N \right\}$, where $ \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n:=|\real (\tilde \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n)| +|\ima (\tilde \lambda^{( \hat x)}_n)|$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Compute the eigendecomposition of (F^{(\hat x)})_# directly (or of its square root) instead of deriving it from eigenvalues of F.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical algorithm as described may use incorrect eigenvalues/eigenvectors for the indicator functions, undermining the stated numerical implementation.
issues.title: Incorrect eigenvalue relation for F_#
issues.why_classification: A short local correction (direct eigendecomposition) preserves all substantive theoretical and numerical goals.
